title: AI app builders for prototypes
summary: Evaluate a demo together with its handoff and operating responsibilities.

sections.heading: Define a prototype that can fail
paragraphs: Use a form, a stored record and an authenticated route. Specify invalid inputs and unauthorized access as well as the happy path. A convincing screenshot does not demonstrate that any of these constraints hold.

sections.heading: Choose a trial path
paragraphs: Inspect Lovable for a natural-language web workflow, Bolt for its documented JavaScript path, and Replit for an agent-assisted app workflow. Confirm the actual framework and operating requirements in the sources rather than assuming interchangeability.

sections.heading: Handoff is an acceptance criterion
paragraphs: Ask another developer to build from the exported code and configuration instructions. Inventory databases, domains, secrets and service accounts. If the project cannot be handed over, count that as a constraint even when the initial demo is impressive.

verdict: Pick the builder whose output you can inspect, export and operate after the demo.
bestFor: Founders testing an app idea with an explicit code handoff
notFor: Teams with unresolved mandatory data, security or deployment requirements
migration: Trial the candidate on a branch; retain the original workflow until tests, export and billing checks pass.

pros.text: Bolt documents JavaScript-based web app creation plus a distinct Expo path for mobile prototypes.
Lovable documents code synchronization with Git providers, which gives a prototype a documented repository handoff path.

cons.text: Lovable code synchronization is not the same as moving a database, hosting setup or connected services; those need a separate migration plan.
Replit checkpoints cover an in-platform recovery path; they do not demonstrate independent deployment or recovery from an exported project.

faqs.question: Which documented path fits a JavaScript web or Expo prototype?
faqs.answer: Bolt describes JavaScript-based web frameworks and an Expo mobile route. Confirm the exact framework, dependencies and external services before starting.

faqs.question: What should a prototype handoff test prove?
faqs.answer: Verify that another developer can obtain the code and reproduce the app, then check databases and runtime services separately. Lovable documents Git sync but separates that from service migration.

faqs.question: What should I verify about Lovable model training before sending project code?
faqs.answer: Its 2026-09-15 Privacy Policy says Customer Content and Usage Data may be used for training, with a free settings opt-out that takes effect prospectively on any plan; it excludes Business/Enterprise content and usage data and app end-user data. The August 2026 Terms and November 2025 DPA distinguish data scopes differently, so verify the actual workspace agreement and setting.

faqs.question: Does choosing an EU Lovable Cloud region keep all project data in the EU?
faqs.answer: Lovable says Lovable Cloud offers EU, US and Asia Pacific regions and that selected-region Cloud data does not move across regions by default. Its Privacy Policy also says Lovable and service providers process Personal Data in multiple countries, including the US. This does not establish the actual workspace selection or locations for connected services and model providers.
